## Available source templates

The editable files live in the repository's top-level `templates/` directory.

| Template | Source file | Intended record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard or policy | `standard-or-policy.md` | Approved standards, policies, or principles |
| Guide or best practice | `guide-or-best-practice.md` | Practical guidance, patterns, and tutorials |
| Testing practice | `testing-practice.md` | A discipline-specific practice page |
| Code snippet | `code-snippet.md` | Reusable code with context and limitations |
| Tool or repository | `tool-or-repository.md` | An owned resource reference |
| Checklist | `checklist.md` | A scoped, reviewable checklist |
| Meeting or recording | `meeting-or-recording.md` | Notes, recordings, actions, and materials |
| Decision record | `decision-record.md` | Context, options, outcome, and consequences |
| Proposal or roadmap item | `proposal-or-roadmap-item.md` | A visible idea or planned change |

## How to use a template

1. Copy the closest source template into the appropriate directory under `src/content/docs/`.
2. Rename it with a short, lowercase, hyphen-separated filename.
3. Replace every `TODO` and keep uncertain statements visibly marked.
4. Add the new page to navigation only when it should be discoverable.
5. Run `npm run check` and `npm run build` before requesting review.

The contribution and approval model is still pending. See [Contribute](../contribute/) for the current neutral workflow.

## Future checklist library

Reserved for QA-authored test plans, test cases, exploratory charters, bug reports, release checks, automation proposals, and additional document types. No example checklist is an active company requirement.
